sources.title: Conditions

observedFacts: A tourist eligible for the VAT Refund for Tourists (VRT) scheme must: (1) not hold Thai nationality, (2) not be an airline crew member departing Thailand on duty, and (3) depart Thailand from an international airport.

Goods must be purchased from stores displaying the "VAT REFUND FOR TOURISTS" sign; the amount must be at least THB 2,000 (VAT-inclusive) per store per day, and goods must be taken out of Thailand within 60 days of the date of purchase.
At departure, the traveler must present the goods and a VAT Refund Application form (P.P.10) with original tax invoices to Customs for stamping before check-in.

Luxury goods — the official page explicitly lists jewelry, gold ornaments, watches, glasses/eyeglasses, and pens — require an additional inspection by Revenue Department officers at the VAT Refund for Tourists counter in the departure lounge, after passing immigration, in addition to the Customs stamp.

Refunds up to THB 30,000 may be paid in cash (Baht), by bank draft, or credited to a credit card; claims are submitted at the airport VAT Refund counter, or the documents may be mailed to the Revenue Department.
limitations: The official pages describe the general VRT process and do not themselves confirm that any specific Rolex authorized retailer in Thailand participates in the VRT sign-up scheme.
The exact processing fee/administrative charge deducted from the refund amount was not located on the pages reviewed and is not recorded here.
Watches are explicitly named as a 'luxury goods' category subject to the additional in-person inspection step; this project's price data does not track which specific retailers participate.
